Brodway Plumbing, Associated Piping Services Inc., and Modern Plumbing Industries stand out as strong options for water heater repair or replacement in Orlando, FL, based on ratings, specialization, review volume, and local service.
Top Recommendations
• Brodway Plumbing (Kissimmee-based, serves Orlando and Central Florida): Frequently highlighted for water heater work. It is a top-rated Rheem authorized service provider specializing in tank, tankless, and hybrid systems (also works with Rinnai, Navien, AO Smith, Bradford White). Ratings are strong (around 4.8–4.9 across Angi/HomeAdvisor with 300+ reviews and high Google ratings with hundreds of reviews). Customers often note professional installs, fair pricing, and same-day service. Phone: [phone removed]. Website: brodwayplumbing.com. Hours are typically Mon–Fri 7 AM–5:30 PM (closed weekends), with online booking. License example referenced: CFC1429985.
• Associated Piping Services Inc. (Orlando): Ranked highly in local directories (e.g., ServiceAgent top pick with ~4.9 stars from 200+ reviews). Family-owned since 1986; handles plumbing (including water heaters) and HVAC. Positive feedback on professionalism, problem-solving, and reliability. Phone: [phone removed]. Address: 1023 29th St, Orlando, FL 32805. Some listings note 24-hour availability.
• Modern Plumbing Industries (Winter Springs, serves greater Orlando): Family-owned since 1975 with a strong focus on water heater repair, maintenance, installation, and replacement (tank, tankless, hybrid). Offers 24-hour service. High review volume (1,000+ on Google in some reports) and A+ BBB mentions. Phone: [phone removed]. Website: modernpi.com.
Other Notable Options
• ABC Plumbing, Air, Heat & Electric: Long-established (since ~1948), high Angi ratings (~4.9 with 600+ reviews), free estimates, and emergency services for water heaters.
• Shamrock Plumbing or similar 24/7 providers: Good for true emergencies (leaking tank, no hot water at odd hours); they emphasize rapid response for water heater failures.
• Others with positive mentions: The Flush Club (strong Thumbtack feedback for emergency repairs), Herrell Plumbing (established since 1970, 24/7), Teles Plumbing, and Drain Genie.
Practical Tips
• For emergencies (leaking tank, flooding, or complete failure): Prioritize companies advertising 24/7 service. Shut off the water supply and power/gas to the unit first to limit damage.
• Get 2–3 quotes: Diagnostic/service call fees often run $100–250; tank water heater replacement commonly $1,100–1,800 (tankless higher). Ask about warranties, same-day availability, and whether they haul away the old unit.
• Verify before hiring: Confirm current Florida plumbing license (CFC number), insurance, and recent reviews on Google, Angi, or Yelp. Check for manufacturer certifications if you have a specific brand (e.g., Rheem).
• Maintenance note: Annual flushing can extend life; many pros offer this.
Start with Brodway if you want a water-heater specialist, or Associated/Modern for broader established local service and potential after-hours help. Call a few promptly—response times and availability can vary by day and demand.
